title: Embedding headroom estimator + cross-tenant QoS shaping for reranking/embeddings
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Problem: The embeddings and reranking endpoints show highly variable p95 latency under mixed tenant loads. Small tenants experience headroom starvation when a few noisy tenants burst, and our current autoscaler reacts too late because it uses request counts instead of token throughput. This ticket scopes an end-to-end approach: (1) a headroom estimator that predicts available embedding throughput per worker pool, (2) per-tenant QoS shaping with soft-budgets and burst tokens, and (3) a token-aware autoscaler that scales based on effective token/sec demand and observed p95 latency signals. Target: reduce cross-tenant p95 latency variance by 40% and cut customer-impacting queue time for small tenants by 60% under 2x burst scenarios.
implementation_plan: 1) Instrument: add token_count and effective_sequence_length to embedding router metrics and per-tenant request traces. 2) Headroom estimator: build a lightweight estimator service (stateless windowed estimator) that consumes worker telemetry and returns available token/sec headroom per pool. 3) QoS shaping: implement per-tenant leaky-bucket queues with configurable soft_budget and burst_tokens; requests above soft budget receive delayed scheduling or graceful degradation (quantized model fallback) based on policy. 4) Autoscaler: replace request-count autoscaling rule for embeddings with token/sec + latency P90/P95 feedback loop (PID controller with minimum ramp-up delay). 5) Tests: synthetic multi-tenant load tests and chaos experiments (node drain) in staging. 6) Rollout: gradual rollout with canary tenant gating and throttles enabled behind a feature flag.
acceptance_criteria:
- p95 latency variance across tenants reduced >= 40% in benchmark harness (same scenarios as baseline).
- Small-tenant median queue wait <= 50ms under 2x noisy tenant burst.
- Autoscaler scales up within target window (scale decision within 30s of sustained token/sec increase) without oscillation in 95% of synthetic runs.
- Feature flag and fallback policies documented; QA runbook updated.
- Grafana dashboards show headroom estimator accuracy (within 15% of measured capacity) for 24h after rollout.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): enable full instrumentation and headroom estimator; run end-to-end integration with load harness. Phase 2 (canary): enable QoS shaping and autoscaler for 5% of production tenants (low-risk group), monitor for 48h. Phase 3 (ramp): +25% tenants each 24h pending green metrics. Phase 4: global enable with fallbacks to quantized model and region-level throttling if aggregate latency regresses. Feature flag controls: embedding.qos_shaping.enabled, embedding.headroom.enabled, embedding.autoscaler.token_mode.
monitoring: New Grafana panels: embedding_pool_headroom (token/sec), per_tenant_soft_budget_usage, embedding_queue_wait_ms (p50/p90/p95), autoscaler_decision_events, regeneration_fallback_rate. Alerts: p95 latency > 600ms for >5m AND fallback_rate > 0.5% => pager. Alert playbook: revert feature flag, temporary rate-limits, contact infra on suspected capacity mis-estimation.
risks:
- Headroom estimator may under- or over-estimate capacity during heterogeneous model mixes (different quantization/sequence length). Mitigation: conservative headroom floor and model-specific multipliers.
- QoS shaping could introduce unfairness if soft budgets misconfigured. Mitigation: rolling out with conservative defaults and telemetry.
- Autoscaler tuning risk: oscillation or slow response. Mitigation: PID parameter sweep in staging and minimum/maximum replica constraints.
comments: 2025-01-12 Sofia Patel: Initial spike analysis attached to design doc. Noted two major failure modes: (A) short token bursts causing worker saturation, (B) long sequences consuming disproportionate KV memory and reducing throughput.

2025-01-20 Lucas Nguyen: Prototype estimator implemented. Using 60s sliding window and per-model capacity coefficients. Early numbers look promising in staging (headroom estimate within ~12% of measured). PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/782
2025-01-28 Priya Shah (SRE): Observability additions look good; requesting an alert to differentiate estimator drift vs actual capacity losses (node failure). Added alert stubs to playbook.
